hook.text: Ask riders what matters most. Speed? Comfort? No—it's how long they wait for the next bus or train.

buildup.text: A bus every 30 minutes feels unreliable. A bus every 10 minutes feels like a system you can trust.

discovery.text: Frequency is freedom. At 10-minute headways, you don't need a schedule—you just show up and go.

twist.text: High frequency costs money. Each added trip requires fuel, driver time, and vehicle maintenance.

climax.text: The most successful transit cities invest in frequency above all else. Everything else follows.

punchline.text: Frequency is the single best predictor of ridership.

quiz.question: Why is frequency more important than speed in transit?
options: Short waits let riders skip schedules and just show up
